nodes.label: Bridge: Interdependent Parallel Generation
nodes.rationale: Proposes architectural modification allowing N parallel LLM generations to share information via attention on batch axis, improving reasoning performance with only 2.8-5.1% new parameters.

nodes.label: Bridge Blocks: Cross-Sequence Attention
nodes.rationale: Attention mechanism operating on batch axis (B×S×D tensor) rather than sequence axis, enabling tokens from same prompt to attend to each other. Markovian design without key-value cache.

nodes.label: RLVR Training with Bridge
nodes.rationale: SFT warm-up on correct reasoning traces followed by GRPO training with verifiable rewards. Bridge blocks introduce inter-sample dependence in advantage computation.

nodes.label: Math Reasoning Benchmarks (MATH, AIME, AMC, etc.)
nodes.rationale: Evaluation on MATH-500, AIME24, AIME25, AMC23, BRUMO25, CMIMC25, HMMT_FEB25 plus non-math tasks (XSum, CNN/DailyMail, GPQA, ZebraLogic, Countdown).

nodes.label: Parallel Inference Scaling for LLMs
nodes.rationale: Scaling inference compute by generating N>1 responses per prompt. Independent generations waste information; Bridge enables interdependence while maintaining parallelism.

nodes.label: Axial Attention in Transformers
nodes.rationale: Attention on different axes of high-order tensors. Bridge applies attention on batch axis (cross-sequence) rather than sequence axis, treating B×S×D as structured tensor.

hyperedges.label: Parallel Generation with Information Sharing
hyperedges.rationale: Bridge enables N parallel generations to share information via cross-sequence attention (axial attention on batch axis), improving reasoning quality while maintaining parallelism. Addresses limitation of independent parallel sampling.
